title: Education
description: Words for discussing schools, universities, teaching methods and lifelong learning in Writing Task 2 and Speaking.

words.definition: the subjects and content taught in a school or course
words.example: Many educators believe financial literacy should be part of the national curriculum.

words.definition: required by law or a rule
words.example: In some countries, learning a second language is compulsory from primary school.

words.definition: money paid for teaching at a college or university
words.example: Rising tuition fees discourage many talented students from going to university.

words.definition: learning by repeating information until it is memorised, without understanding it
words.example: Critics argue that rote learning does little to develop students' critical thinking.

words.definition: the ability to analyse information carefully and form judgements
words.example: Debating clubs are an excellent way to develop critical thinking.

words.definition: the ability to read and write, or knowledge of a particular subject
words.example: Adult literacy rates have risen sharply over the past three decades.

words.definition: providing skills and training for a particular job
words.example: Vocational courses can offer a faster route into skilled employment than a degree.

words.definition: how well a student does in their studies
words.example: Research shows that sleep has a strong influence on academic performance.

words.definition: done in addition to normal school lessons
words.example: Extracurricular activities such as sport and music help children build confidence.

words.definition: to officially join a course, school or university
words.example: More adults are enrolling in online courses to update their skills.

words.definition: to leave school or a course before finishing it
words.example: Financial pressure forces some students to drop out of university in their first year.

words.definition: the methods and practice of teaching
words.example: Modern pedagogy places greater emphasis on collaboration than on lectures.

words.definition: studying from home with materials or classes provided online or by post
words.example: Distance learning allows people in remote villages to earn recognised qualifications.

words.definition: an experienced person who advises and supports a less experienced person
words.example: Having a mentor in the first year of university can make a huge difference.

words.definition: an official record that you have passed exams or completed a course
words.example: Employers increasingly look for experience as well as formal qualifications.

words.definition: the practice of making people obey rules and behave well
words.example: Some parents feel that schools are no longer strict enough about discipline.

words.definition: connected with thinking, learning and understanding
words.example: Learning a musical instrument may boost children's cognitive development.

words.definition: exams given to all students in the same way and marked in the same way
words.example: Critics claim that standardised testing encourages teachers to teach only to the exam.

words.definition: having a natural ability or high intelligence
words.example: Gifted children may become bored if lessons are not challenging enough.

words.definition: continuing to learn throughout one's life
words.example: In a fast-changing job market, lifelong learning is no longer optional.

words.definition: a university student studying for a first degree
words.example: Most undergraduates now combine their studies with part-time work.

words.definition: money given to a student to help pay for their education
words.example: She won a full scholarship to study engineering in Australia.

words.definition: to judge the quality, ability or value of someone or something
words.example: Students are assessed through a combination of coursework and final exams.

words.definition: the level of success achieved, especially in education
words.example: There is still a large gap in educational attainment between rural and urban students.

words.definition: involving active participation and practical experience
words.example: Science is easier to understand through hands-on experiments than through textbooks.

words.definition: copying someone else's work and presenting it as your own
words.example: Universities use software to detect plagiarism in student essays.

words.definition: having a wide range of skills, interests and experiences
words.example: Schools should aim to produce well-rounded individuals, not just high exam scores.

words.definition: a department of a university, or all the teaching staff
words.example: The faculty of medicine has introduced a new training programme.

words.definition: including and welcoming all types of people, including those with disabilities
words.example: Inclusive classrooms allow children with special needs to learn alongside their peers.

words.definition: the influence that people of the same age or group have on each other's behaviour
words.example: Teenagers often start smoking because of peer pressure rather than genuine interest.
